transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-01
Time: 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Novus CTO), Priya Nair (Novus Head of ML), Carlos Ruiz (Novus Eng Lead)
Links shared: pricing spreadsheet (drive.redwood/pricing-novus), SOC2 report (redwood.com/soc2), sample benchmark spreadsheet (sheets.redwood/bench-novus)

Summary: quick discovery to surface Novus's p95 latency targets for a fraud-scoring use case, expected concurrency and streaming needs, and whether Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private makes sense. Customer wants to run token/sec benchmarks with their workload and get a recommendation on batching, caching, and quantization for cost vs latency tradeoffs.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm maya from redwood on the A E side, with ravi our se. how's everyone doing?
[00:08] Jordan: good, thanks. morning for me, afternoon for you. this is Jordan, CTO at Novus. we'll be fairly focused on latency and throughput today.
[00:15] Priya: hi, priya here, head of ml — we own the fraud model infra and the scoring pipeline.
[00:19] Carlos: carlos, eng lead on payments. i'll be implementing whatever we decide.
[00:23] Ravi: great, i'll ask a few technical things; we can sketch a benchmark plan by the end. quick note, transcript may spell out things weirdly, forgive auto captions.
[00:30] Jordan: yeah that's fine. quick context: we have a real-time fraud scoring endpoint — presently on our infra — around 1200 RPS at peak, average request has a 600 token prompt after template + metadata. our SLO is p95 <= 150ms for scoring latency, and we need to support up to 500 concurrent scoring requests.
[00:55] Maya: okay p95 150ms and 500 concurrency. are those hard limits or aspirational?
[00:59] Jordan: hard for customer-facing flows. for internal bulk jobs we can be slower, but the card-present flows must be snappy.
[01:06] Priya: also want streaming, because we stream incremental risk signals back to UI — small token streams but they need sub-200ms chunk latency.
[01:15] Ravi: good. couple of clarifying q's: what's your model family — size / fp16 / quantized? and are you planning to host model weights in-cloud or want private on-prem?
[01:25] Priya: currently we're using an open LLM finetuned in fp16, around 7B params, and we've experimented with int8 quantization with gains but some quality drift. we're open to hosting options; data residency is a concern for some EU customers — might require VPC/private deployment.
[01:40] Maya: perfect. to align: we have three deployment modes — Hosted (fast to start, multi-tenant), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools, predictable throughput), Private (VPC or on-prem for compliance). For p95 150ms at 500 concurrency, Hosted might be tight unless we use a lower-latency model variant or aggressive batching/caching. Dedicated or Private with pinned capacity typically gives better p95 predictability.
[02:03] Jordan: can you explain what you mean by batching — we usually think batching increases latency because you wait for batch to fill.
[02:10] Ravi: yeah great question. with Redwood's runtime we do continuous batching and dynamic latency targets. you can set an upper latency SLO and the runtime will send partials/streaming while batching to improve tokens/sec. so you can maintain p95 while still getting throughput benefits. also prefix/KV caching helps for repeated contexts in fraud scoring.
[02:29] Carlos: prefix caching — do you mean caching the key/value cache per session? our sessions have repeated merchant metadata and some user context.
[02:35] Ravi: exactly. KV cache reuse across similar prompts can shave a lot off the first-token cost for long contexts. we also provide model variants — e.g., quantized int8 builds that are cheaper and often slightly faster but you need to validate quality for fraud decisions.
[02:48] Priya: quality is critical. we can't accept false positives that degrade UX. we can do eval sets on our side. what kind of token/sec numbers should we expect per GPU?
[02:56] Ravi: depends on GPU. ballpark: for a 7B model on an A100-ish instance in fp16 you might see 600-1200 tokens/sec single-streaming throughput depending on sequence length and kernel selection; with continuous batching across many concurrent requests that can rise to tens of thousands tokens/sec per GPU. quantized builds on newer GPUs (L40-ish) push further.
[03:17] Jordan: p95 150ms, 500 concurrency — what's the math to figure how many GPUs we'd need?
[03:23] Ravi: rough calc: assume each request generates ~100 tokens on average. at 500 concurrent, if each request is handled serially that's 50k tokens outstanding. to meet 150ms p95 you'd need each token produced in <0.15s / 100 ~ 1.5ms per token which is unrealistic; so we typically use streaming and incremental scoring so each chunk is small. But more practical approach: plan for dedicated capacity sized by latency-sensitive tail — likely tens of GPUs (depends heavily on model, GPU type, quantization). we should run a token/sec benchmark with your workload to get precise numbers.
[03:55] Priya: right — we can provide a representative workload and histograms of sequence lengths.
[03:59] Maya: excellent. we'll run a benchmark and include both hosted and dedicated configs. Hosted we'll prototype on a compatible model variant and measure p95 at your concurrency; Dedicated we'll provision reserved GPUs and test full throughput. For Private, if you need on-prem we can provide an appliance-style plan but that's longer lead time.
[04:16] Carlos: any thoughts on networking? VPC peering latency matters for us, we prefer colocated infra with our payment gateways.
[04:22] Ravi: yes, for p95 under ~200ms network adds matter. Dedicated in the same cloud region reduces RTT; for lowest-latency, Private in your VPC avoids public transit and is preferable. we also support local routing and model copies in region.
[04:34] Jordan: okay. security — do you have KMS integration and audit logs? we're PCI scoped and need strict key management.
[04:40] Maya: we do. SOC2, ISO, KMS/HSM integrations, SAML SSO and RBAC. i'll send the SOC2 report and our KM integrations doc — see link in notes.
[04:49] Priya: what's the typical setup time for a benchmark? we want a quick turnaround.
[04:53] Ravi: we can spin up a controlled benchmark within a few days for Hosted and Dedicated if we have your workload and a runbook. Private/on-prem takes longer — a few weeks maybe.
[05:02] Jordan: we also want canary/fallback behavior — if a dedicated pool is saturated we want to fall back to a cheaper hosted variant to avoid dropped requests. do you support that?
[05:09] Ravi: yes — smart routing can failover by policy to model variants or regions. you can specify latency or cost policies and automatic fallbacks. that helps maintain availability but you need to be okay with potential small quality differences.
[05:21] Carlos: one more: what about quantization quality testing — do you help run A/B evals?
[05:25] Maya: our Optimize toolkit gives quantization recommendations and we can run quality monitoring against your eval set; SE will coordinate the eval pipeline with your tests.
[05:34] Priya: great. for the benchmark, our p95 definition is the end-to-end time from request arrival to first meaningful token delivered to UI. we need p95 <= 150ms for 95% of production traffic. we can share anonymized logs.
[05:47] Ravi: perfect. for the benchmark we'll instrument the same timing points and stream responses so we replicate your metric. we'll also test streaming chunk latency, and token/sec under bursty traffic patterns.
[05:59] Jordan: curious about cost — do you have guidance on cost per 1M tokens for Hosted vs Dedicated?
[06:03] Maya: i'll send the pricing sheet but short answer: Hosted is usage-based and can be higher per token at low volume but low ops overhead. Dedicated is committed capacity and cheaper per-token if you fully utilize GPUs. We can model it for your expected QPS and concurrency.
[06:16] Priya: how do you handle KV cache invalidation — our contexts change per user frequently.
[06:21] Ravi: you control cache keys and TTLs. we provide primitives for session-based caching and manual invalidation. for fraud scoring it's often beneficial to cache merchant-level context and rehydrate user-specific fields to keep cache hit rates high.
[06:33] Carlos: any gotchas with streaming and concurrency? we've seen token interleaving issues before.
[06:38] Ravi: we stream per-request; the runtime guarantees output ordering per request. interleaving happens only across multiplexed channels if you misuse the stream, but we provide SDKs with correct concurrency semantics.
[06:51] Jordan: can we get a simple pilot: hosted test to validate p95 at reduced load and a dedicated benchmark to extrapolate to full load?
[06:58] Maya: absolutely. proposed plan: 1) Redwoods sends pricing + SOC2 + benchmark plan; 2) Novus provides workload sample, histogram, and target metric definitions; 3) SE-run hosted pilot within 3 business days, dedicated benchmark within 7 business days; 4) review results and decide Dedicated vs Private. does that timeline work?
[07:17] Priya: yes, sounds good. we'll try to provide the workload by Friday.
[07:21] Maya: perfect. any other questions?
[07:24] Carlos: one: are there limits on streaming chunk sizes or throughput per connection?
[07:28] Ravi: no hard limits — SDKs stream small chunks. we recommend chunk sizes of 8-32 tokens for low-latency UI updates. throughput per connection is bounded by network, but the runtime multiplexes well.
[07:40] Jordan: are there examples of customers hitting sub-200ms p95 with streaming?
[07:44] Maya: yes, we have retail and payments customers who've hit p95 ~120-180ms with dedicated pools + kv caching. i'll include anonymized benchmark notes.
[07:53] Priya: ok let's wrap. recap and next steps?
[07:57] Maya: recap: we heard p95 150ms target, 500 concurrency, streaming for UI, interest in Dedicated with potential Private for EU residency. next steps in notes — i'll send pricing, SOC2, benchmark plan; Ravi will own the benchmark execution; Priya will send workload.
[08:12] Jordan: thanks all. looking forward to the benchmark.
[08:15] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email and schedule the technical deep dive.

End of transcript.
